title: Amortized Min Deque
description:
Design a double-ended queue `MinDeque` using **two min-stacks** that supports insertions and removals at **both ends** as well as retrieving the current minimum element, all in **amortized `O(1)` time** per operation.

Implement the `MinDeque` class:
- `MinDeque()` initializes an empty deque.
- `void pushFront(int val)` inserts `val` at the front of the deque.
- `void pushBack(int val)` inserts `val` at the back of the deque.
- `int popFront()` removes and returns the front element.
- `int popBack()` removes and returns the back element.
- `int getMin()` returns the minimum element currently in the deque.
constraints: Methods popFront, popBack, and getMin are always called on non-empty deques.
At most 5 * 10^4 calls will be made across all methods.
hints: Maintain two min-stacks: `left` (whose top is the deque front) and `right` (whose top is the deque back), so `getMin()` is simply `min(left.min, right.min)`.

When popping from an empty stack while the other stack has `m` elements, move only the bottom `ceil(m / 2)` elements (reversed) to the empty stack and rebuild prefix minimums on both halves; by potential `||left| - |right||`, every operation is amortized O(1).

examples.explanation: Deque becomes [3, 5, 1] (min 1); popBack removes 1 -> [3, 5] (min 3); popFront removes 3 -> [5] (min 5).
Pushing 10, 20, 30 to back then alternating popFront (10) and popBack (30) leaves [20] with min 20.
Single element pushed to front can be popped from back cleanly.
